wu: Weekend Plans Bingo: Students write 5 weekend activities on a bingo grid. Teacher calls out activities (e.g., 'play football', 'visit family'). Students mark off and shout 'Bingo!' when complete, then share one plan.
wuAlt: Two Stars and a Wish: Students share one good thing and one wish for the weekend, then guess a partner's plans.
Quick Poll: Teacher asks 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Students raise hands for options like 'study', 'play games', 'go out'.
pres: Show flashcards of weekend activities (e.g., 'visit grandma', 'study English', 'play football'). Model sentences: 'I'm going to visit grandma on Saturday.' Elicit time expressions ('on Saturday', 'in the evening'). Check understanding by asking 'What are YOU going to do?'
presAlt: Plan Grid Poster: Draw a 3x3 grid on the board with 'Saturday morning', 'Saturday afternoon', etc. Fill in plans with 'going to' and elicit from students.
Dialogue Roleplay: Teacher and a student act out a conversation about weekend plans using 'going to' and time expressions.
prac: Plan Grid Mingle: Students receive a half-filled grid with time slots (e.g., 'Saturday morning'). They mingle, ask 'What are you going to do [time]?', and write partners' answers. Swap grids and repeat.
pracAlt: Going-To Fortune Teller: Students fold paper into a fortune teller, write activities inside. They ask partners 'What are you going to do?' and lift flaps to reveal 'predictions'.
Sentence Relay: Teams race to write correct 'going to' sentences on the board for prompts like 'Sunday / clean room'.
ls: Plan Swap Listening: Students listen to 3 audio clips of teens talking about weekend plans. They match each speaker to a time slot on a handout (e.g., 'Speaker 1: Saturday afternoon / Speaker 2: Sunday morning').
re: Action Charades: Teacher mimes an activity (e.g., 'swimming'). Students shout 'You're going to swim!' and mime the action. Fast-paced to re-energize.
prod: Holiday Plans Survey: Students interview 3 partners using 'What are you going to do during the next holiday?'. They tally responses (e.g., '2 students: visit family') and share findings with the class.
rw: Read and Underline: Students read a short text about a teen's holiday plans (e.g., 'I'm going to travel to Agadir with my family. We're going to swim and eat seafood.'). They underline all 'going to' phrases and write 1 new sentence about their own holiday.
st: Sing 'What Are You Going to Do?' (to the tune of 'Frère Jacques') with actions. End with: 'Today we learned to talk about future plans with going to. Thank you, class! Goodbye!'
g: Students swap written weekend plans and correct errors using 'going to'.
Match activity cards to time expression cards (e.g., 'watch a movie' + 'Saturday evening').
Students sit in a circle and build a sentence: 'I'm going to play football on Saturday. What are YOU going to do?'
Cut up a 'going to' sentence and students reassemble it correctly.
Students draw emojis for activities and write sentences: 'I'm going to 😊 on Sunday.'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 'going to' sentences about a dream holiday.
Support: Use sentence frames: 'I'm going to ___ on ___.' with word bank.
hw: Write 6 sentences about your next weekend using 'going to' and time expressions.
Draw a picture of your weekend plans and label 3 activities with 'going to' sentences.
Interview a family member about their weekend plans and write 2 sentences about them.
tip: Use Moroccan holidays (e.g., Eid, Green March) as examples to make plans culturally relevant and boost engagement.
